json.description: The Wellness Center presents "Beyond the Mirror", a presentation geared towards the challenges of First-Year Student life that is focused on identifying ways to cope with self-image and body image. The St. Olaf Band, conducted by Assistant Professor of Music Henry L. Dorn, will perform its Homecoming and Family Weekend Concert in Skoglund Gymnasium on Saturday, October 3, from 7:30-9 p.m.

Founded in 1891, the St. Olaf Band is the oldest music organization at St. Olaf College, a campus internationally renowned for its high-caliber music ensembles. The band has toured nationally since 1904 and internationally since 1906, when it performed a four-week, 30-concert tour of Norway, making it the first American collegiate band to tour Europe. The band has subsequently toured several times in Norway, Great Britain, Japan, Central Europe, Australia, and New Zealand.

Dr. Soojung Hong has won national and international recognition as a pianist, and performs as a soloist or with ensemble throughout the Midwest and beyond. Her work highlights the music of female composers. See this dedication in her video production of Fanny Mendelssohn’s cycle “Das Jahr” (“The Year”)—supported by the Minnesota State Arts Board’s Artist Initiative Grant— among other notable projects. 

Dr. Hong is also a devoted educator, and many college campuses welcome her master class presentations and competition adjudications. Notably, she serves as Founder and Artist Director for the PianoFun Minnesota Festival, a piano professor at Normandale Community College, and a piano faculty member at MacPhail Center for Music and North Central University.   

This event is free and open to the public.

Of all Shakespeare’s tragedies, Antony and Cleopatra is a hidden gem of contrasts battling against one another. The play centers on one of the world’s most infamous conflicts, during the height of the Roman Empire. It details one of the greatest love affairs in history, between the esteemed Roman general Marc Antony, and the lovely idolized Egyptian queen, Cleopatra. Antony grapples between his intense devotion to Cleopatra and his honor that ties him to his duties as a Roman triumvirate. The balance between his two lives slowly unravels as tensions between the ruling powers of Rome arise. Cleopatra brings the heightened emotions while honor is pitted against love throughout the thrilling action, building the energy of the play to a sorrowfully explosive conclusion. Come find out the fate of these passionate lovers in St. Olaf Shakespeare Troupe’s production of Antony and Cleopatra!

The St. Olaf Festival of Bands, scheduled for October 31, 2026, has enjoyed a long, successful history of bringing together outstanding high school musicians to prepare and share a program with nationally acclaimed artists. An exciting and intense day of rehearsals culminates with performances by the Festival Band, the St. Olaf Band, and the Norseman Band. It promises to be a stimulating day for students and teachers alike.

We are excited to announce that guest clinician Lauren Reynolds will bring her exceptional expertise to lead the Festival Band this year. As associate professor of music and director of concert bands at the University of Delaware School of Music, where she conducts the wind ensemble and teaches conducting and wind literature, Dr. Reynolds is a distinguished leader in the field. Her participation promises to be an inspiring and invaluable experience for all involved.

We will also be joined by Michael Buck, conductor of the Norseman Band. Michael Buck is a 1989 graduate of St. Olaf College and the former director of bands at The College of St. Scholastica in Duluth. We are thrilled about the ongoing impact he is making on music-making at St. Olaf and the Festival of Bands.

SGA is partnering with the Institute of Freedom and Community to host Dinner with 6 Strangers, an event encouraging St. Olaf students to connect with people they may not have otherwise met.   • What are you passionate about? When was the last time you surprised yourself? What did the people who raised you teach you about love? Has a stranger ever changed your life?
